hops.afterHeading: The link that has to fire: what makes the synapse release
hops.title: Hearing that comes and goes with a fever
hops.text: Three siblings, aged 7, 9 and 10, treated in Paris, had at most mild baseline pure-tone loss, with impaired speech discrimination, and severe or profound loss during fever; their mother reported recovery took three to four days after the fever broke. Their electrophysiology showed an auditory neuropathy: an abnormal brainstem response, with otoacoustic emissions still present. Marlin and colleagues linked it to a single deleted amino acid in a calcium-binding C2 domain of otoferlin. In mice homozygous for Ile515Thr, another otoferlin variant tied to temperature-sensitive hearing loss in people, a Gottingen group found 65 percent less otoferlin in inner hair cells than controls and much weaker release during prolonged stimulation.

sources.citation: Marlin S, Feldmann D, Nguyen Y, et al. Temperature-sensitive auditory neuropathy associated with an otoferlin mutation: Deafening fever! Biochem Biophys Res Commun. 2010;394(3):737-742.
Strenzke N, Chakrabarti R, Al-Moyed H, et al. Hair cell synaptic dysfunction, auditory fatigue and thermal sensitivity in otoferlin Ile515Thr mutants. EMBO J. 2016;35(23):2519-2535.
Forli F, Lazzerini F, Auletta G, et al. Temperature-sensitive auditory neuropathy spectrum disorder: a case report and literature review. 2023.

hops.afterHeading: Putting the link back: a gene too big for its vector
hops.title: The virus that was first found as a contaminant
hops.text: In 1965, Atchison, Casto and Hammon separated tiny DNA-containing particles from preparations of a monkey adenovirus. On their own the particles would not replicate in culture; they multiplied only when an adenovirus was inoculated alongside them, so the authors called them defective. Those particles are adeno-associated virus, and the shell is still cramped. In one packaging series, efficiency was best from 4.1 to 4.9 kilobases and dropped sharply above that; a second team detected no packaged genome longer than 5.2 kilobases, and its oversized constructs gave fragments. Dong's team also found that when the vector genome was less than half the wild-type length, each capsid held two copies.

sources.citation: Atchison RW, Casto BC, Hammon WM. Adenovirus-associated defective virus particles. Science. 1965;149(3685):754-756.
Dong JY, Fan PD, Frizzell RA. Quantitative analysis of the packaging capacity of recombinant adeno-associated virus. Hum Gene Ther. 1996;7(17):2101-2112.
Wu Z, Yang H, Colosi P. Effect of genome size on AAV vector packaging. Mol Ther. 2010;18(1):80-86.

image.caption: Found in 1965 as a defective hitchhiker, AAV still has room for only a short cassette.

hops.afterHeading: Reading an early-phase trial without inflating it
hops.title: Zero decibels is not silence
hops.text: Zero on a hearing chart sounds like total silence, which makes a threshold of minus ten look like a misprint. On the hearing-level scale, zero is the level a healthy young adult is expected to just detect, and normal hearing runs from minus ten to twenty dB HL. At the 1939 World's Fairs the Bell System built its own young-adult reference: rooms seating seven, fading phonograph tones through a telephone receiver, 550,000 photographed scorecards, and zero set at the mean for visitors aged 20 to 29, close to the audiometer zero already in use. Score better than the reference and your threshold goes negative.

sources.citation: Steinberg JC, Montgomery HC, Gardner MB. Results of the World's Fair hearing tests. Bell System Technical Journal. 1940;19(4):533-562.
Schnupp J, Nelken I, King A. dB HL, sensitivity to sound, clinical audiograms. Auditory Neuroscience: Making Sense of Sound (MIT Press).

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: Visitors in 1939 attire seated in a wooden listening booth holding vintage telephone receivers to their ears.
image.caption: Audiometric zero is a young-adult reference level, not silence, so sharp ears score negative decibels.
